questions.explain: SQL Server 2025's native vector index is built on DiskANN, a graph-based ANN algorithm designed at Microsoft Research for SSD-backed, billion-scale search.
options: A B-tree variant tuned for high-dimensional data
DiskANN, a graph-based approximate nearest neighbor algorithm
HNSW, the same in-memory graph index used by several dedicated vector databases
A columnstore index over the VECTOR column
questions.q: What indexing algorithm powers SQL Server 2025's native vector index?

questions.explain: A mismatched metric does not error; it silently degrades ranking quality, which is why the chapter stresses the metric must match the model and the queries.
options: The query fails with a metric-mismatch error at execution time
The optimizer automatically rebuilds the index with the correct metric
VECTOR_SEARCH falls back to exact search for that query
The query runs but silently returns poorly ranked results
questions.q: You create a vector index with METRIC = 'cosine' but your queries specify VECTOR_DISTANCE('euclidean', ...). What happens?

questions.explain: In the current preview the table must have a single-column integer clustered key, becomes read-only while the index exists, and partitioned tables, views, and temp tables are not supported.
options: The table becomes read-only while the vector index exists, so ingesting new data means dropping and recreating the index
The index can only be created on tables with a composite clustered primary key
Index builds are fully online and resumable
Partitioned tables, views, and temporary tables are all supported

questions.explain: Under roughly 50,000 vectors exact search is so fast that the DiskANN index buys almost nothing while adding build time and write-path friction.
options: 1,000 vectors
10,000 vectors
50,000 vectors
1,000,000 vectors

questions.explain: The standard methodology is a scheduled spot-check: run representative queries through both the exact and approximate paths and compute the fraction of the exact top-k present in the approximate top-k.
options: Compare VECTOR_SEARCH results against exact VECTOR_DISTANCE ground truth on a sample of query vectors, on a schedule
Divide the TOP_N value by the number of index partitions
Read the recall estimate from sys.dm_exec_query_stats
Count the logical reads of the VECTOR_SEARCH plan and compare them to the exact plan
